items.title: Officers Misjudged Jamal Francique's Walking Pace Before Arrest Turned Into Takedown, Inquest Told
items.summary: According to testimony at the coroner's inquest into the police shooting death of Jamal Francique, Peel Regional Police detective Jason Sweeting said officers failed to anticipate several factors in their 2020 arrest plan, including Francique's prior victimization. Sweeting testified that Francique walked from his home to his car faster than officers expected, delaying their response. Police had planned to block Francique's vehicle with an unmarked car once he reached it, believing they could arrest him first, according to the inquest. Instead, the operation turned into a high risk takedown after Francique entered his vehicle and put it into motion, the inquest heard. The shooting took place outside a townhouse complex on the evening of Jan. 7, 2020. The inquest also heard there was no urgency to rush the arrest, since Francique had only breached bail conditions days earlier.

items.title: Cedar Tree Circles, Didukh-Making and Mocktail Classes Headline CreativeHub 1352's December Workshop Lineup
items.summary: According to CreativeHub 1352, a new slate of hands-on workshops will run alongside the Mississauga Festival of Trees at the Small Arms Inspection Building from Dec. 4 to 13. The non-profit says the lineup includes an Indigenous Cedar Tree Circle, a session on the Ukrainian tradition of Didukh-making, and a candle-making class. Organizers say other sessions let participants try soft pastels, acrylic painting, needle felting, embroidery and letter writing. CreativeHub 1352 says wellness options are also on offer, including morning yoga, a clarifying face mask workshop and a tasting of Himalayan tartary buckwheat. The group says a mocktail-making class is included too, with proceeds supporting its non-profit programming. CreativeHub 1352 notes free drop-in activities will run throughout the festival for anyone who prefers not to register in advance.

items.title: Santa Claus Parade brings holiday lights and festivities back to Mississauga
items.summary: Santa Claus is coming to Mississauga tomorrow (Nov. 21), bringing a parade of illuminated floats, marching bands and holiday entertainment to downtown streets as the city officially kicks off the Christmas season. , with this year’s theme, “Sauga’s Home for the Holidays,” celebrating the people, cultures, traditions and stories that make up the community. Presented by TD, the free event will also feature the first lighting of the city’s Christmas tree at Celebration Square, as Santa’s sleigh makes its way through the downtown core. m. A DJ dance party, food trucks serving festive treats and photo opportunities with Santa and other holiday characters will be available ahead of the parade. m. m. The parade will feature glowing floats, festive walking groups and marching bands playing holiday favourites. Its theme is intended to reflect the many ways people in Mississauga celebrate the season and come together as a community. The procession will travel through City Centre, with Santa passing through Celebration Square to light the Christmas tree. Motorists should prepare for road closures and parking restrictions in the downtown area beginning at noon Saturday. Several streets will be closed at different times as the parade approaches and passes through the route, with roads reopening once it is safe to do so.

items.title: Local Taxpayers Cover Services Gap as Advocates Say Ontario Shortchanges Peel Non-Profits by $1.4 Billion
items.summary: According to Metamorphosis Network coordinator Sean Meagher, Ontario is underfunding non-profits across Mississauga, Brampton and the wider GTA by roughly $1.4 billion, spanning housing, long-term care and addiction services. Meagher told insauga.com funding outside Toronto has not kept pace with demand, and that the Peel shortfall alone stood at $868 million a year as of 2024. He said Metamorphosis data showed the province gives Peel residents $578 less per person annually than comparable regions, noting Toronto is twice Peel's size yet has six times the affordable housing. Meagher said a gap in one area ripples across the system, with local taxpayers covering costs the province should bear. He added that in York Region, that gap rose by $123 million over the past decade. Meagher said roughly 10 per cent of a resident's tax bill funds services the province should cover.

items.title: Long-serving Mississauga library branch celebrates 50th anniversary
items.summary: A Mississauga library branch that has spent five decades serving the community from inside a shopping mall is marking its 50th anniversary with a free family celebration later this month. Sheridan Library, located on the lower level of Sheridan Centre at 2225 Erin Mills Parkway, first opened in 1976. The branch is celebrating the milestone on Saturday, Nov. 28, with an afternoon of entertainment and activities for residents. The anniversary is also a chance to look back at a time when Sheridan Mall was a relatively new addition to the area. The shopping centre opened in 1972, making it one of the first indoor malls in the area. Four years later, the library opened its doors there, giving residents another community resource in a growing part of Mississauga. The branch has remained at the shopping centre throughout its 50-year history, even though its location within the mall has changed. In 2000, Sheridan Library moved to a new space on the mall’s lower level, where it continues to operate today. m. m. m. , including colouring activities and a Lego program. The event is free and open to the public.

items.title: Fourteen Artist-Made Tree Sculptures Explore Sustainable Futures at Mississauga's Returning Festival of Trees
items.summary: According to CreativeHub 1352, the sixth annual Mississauga Festival of Trees returns for 10 days, running Dec. 4 to 13 at the historic Small Arms Inspection Building on Lakeshore Road. The organizers say the event combines art, culture and community through holiday shopping, artist installations, workshops and family activities. At the centre of the festival is an exhibition of 14 tree-themed sculptures commissioned from local artists under this year's theme, Imagining Sustainable Futures, according to CreativeHub 1352. The group says trees will also carry community-made artwork, with two pieces auctioned off to support local arts charities. CreativeHub 1352 says visitors can wander among the sculptures while browsing the market and workshops. The festival also includes a weekend Holiday Market with culinary and artisan vendors selling handcrafted goods and treats, the group says.

items.title: Someone in Mississauga just won a $38 million lottery jackpot
items.summary: Someone in Mississauga is $38 million richer after hitting the Lotto 6/49 Gold Ball jackpot in Wednesday night’s draw. The Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation (OLG) confirmed Thursday that the winning ticket for the Nov. 11 draw was sold in Mississauga, making it one of Ontario’s biggest lottery wins this year. But that wasn’t the only major prize claimed in the province. 30. Meanwhile, another lucky ticket holder in the Leeds and Grenville region won a $1-million Encore prize. The winning Gold Ball number for Wednesday’s draw was 43779735-02, according to OLG’s published results. As for the $38-million winner, their identity has not yet been made public. The winner will need to come forward and have their ticket validated by OLG before officially claiming the life-changing prize. With the next Lotto 6/49 draw taking place Saturday, Nov. 14, there’s another chance for someone to walk away with a life-changing prize.

items.title: Dundas Street Pizza Pizza Ordered Shut, Then Cleared to Reopen Same Day After Peel Recheck
items.summary: According to the Region of Peel, a Pizza Pizza location at 1093 Dundas Street West, near Erindale Station Road, failed a health inspection on Friday, Nov. 13. Health officials say inspectors ordered the restaurant closed immediately after finding infractions during that visit. Records show a follow-up inspection happened later the same day, and the restaurant passed with no infractions outstanding. Peel says the shop was then cleared to reopen for business right away. Inspection records from earlier this year show the same location has faced health issues before, suggesting this was not an isolated incident. The region has not said how long the restaurant stayed closed between the two inspections that day.

items.title: Bamboo Legend's Mississauga Location Set to Shut Its Doors Nov. 26 After More Than Two Decades
items.summary: According to a social media post from Bamboo Legend, the Thai restaurant's Mississauga location at 3145 Dundas St., near Winston Churchill Boulevard, will close its doors on Thursday, Nov. 26, after more than 20 years in business. The family behind the restaurant says they opened their first mom and pop shop in Brampton in 1998, originally serving native Vietnamese cuisine alongside a small Thai menu. The owners say that after travelling to Thailand and studying with Thai chefs, they opened the Mississauga location in 2004, followed by a sister branch in Oakville in 2008. Bamboo Legend did not say why it decided to close the Mississauga location, but hinted at possible future plans in the city. The restaurant thanked loyal neighbourhood regulars, former customers who return for nostalgia, and recent discoveries alike in its announcement.
